title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Snapshot
summary: The 2-Year Treasury yield stood at 3.78% as of April 13, 2026, down 3 basis points from 3.81% on April 10. Recent observations show yields oscillating in a narrow range between 3.78% and 3.81% over the past week.
key_points: Yields have been relatively stable with no directional trend
why_it_matters: The 2-year yield reflects near-term Fed policy expectations and serves as a benchmark for short-term borrowing costs. This data point should be cross-referenced with qualitative sources (FOMC statements, speeches, news) to determine what drove the yield level or changes.
macro_context: As a market-based measure of expected short-term rates, the 2-year Treasury yield provides quantitative context for policy expectations. This raw observation lacks the narrative to determine whether the current level reflects uncertainty, stability, or anticipation of policy shifts.
